article_title: Influence of aging on visual perception and visual motor integration in Korean adults
citation: Kim E, Park Y-K, Byun Y-H, Park M-S, Kim H. (2014). Influence of aging on visual perception and visual motor integration in Korean adults. Journal of Exercise Rehabilitation 10(4):245-250. https://doi.org/10.12965/jer.140147
title: K-DTVP-2 and VMI-3R assessment instruments for visual perception and visual-motor integration
description: Two standardized instruments used to measure age-related change in visual perception and visual-motor integration. The K-DTVP-2 is the Korean version of DTVP-2, consisting of 8 sub-tests such as "eye-hand coordination" and "figure-ground", yielding a General Visual Perception Quotient (mean 100, SD 15) in about 30 to 60 min; its Cronbach's alpha was .883. The VMI-3R involves copying 24 shapes arranged from simplest to most complex, scored 0 to 50 points in 10 to 13 min; its Cronbach's alpha was .641.
requirements: Examiners trained to perform, analyze, and score the results exactly; raw sub-item scores converted to standard scores for interpretation.
constraints: K-DTVP-2 was designed to measure 4 to 8 yr old children's visual perceptual ability; VMI-3R internal consistency (alpha .641) was lower than K-DTVP-2's.
target_learners: Adults aged 20-79 in this study; instruments span preschool children to adults
target_learning_goals: Measuring visual perceptual ability and visual-motor integration to identify cognitive deficit levels
examples: Principal component analysis extracted one factor explaining 57.1% of total variance for K-DTVP-2 and 54.5% for VMI-3R.
key_sources: Kim E, Park Y-K, Byun Y-H, Park M-S, Kim H. (2014). Influence of aging on visual perception and visual motor integration in Korean adults. Journal of Exercise Rehabilitation 10(4):245-250. https://doi.org/10.12965/jer.140147

article_title: "K" EY rules to improve learning skills in forth arm robotic platform.
citation: Bigolin AV, Cavazzola LT, Kalil AN. (2026). “K” EY rules to improve learning skills in forth arm robotic platform. ABCD Arq Bras Cir Dig. https://doi.org/10.1590/0102-67202026000001e1930
title: The "K" technique divides the robotic surgical field into quadrants to coordinate four-arm movement
description: The "K" technique is a mnemonic training method for the four-arm robotic platform. The surgical field is split right/left, and the side with two working arms is divided into three zones — top, middle and bottom — forming "a letter K when on the right side, and an inverted K when on the left". It structures arm activation during swap maneuvers.
requirements: One arm of the platform is dedicated to the optics, and the number of arms on each side determines which surgeon hand commands which forceps
constraints: Described for the da Vinci 4th and 5th generation platform with up to four arms
examples: The technique was developed from training of more than 400 robotic surgeons from different specialties
key_sources: Bigolin AV, Cavazzola LT, Kalil AN. (2026). “K” EY rules to improve learning skills in forth arm robotic platform. ABCD Arq Bras Cir Dig. https://doi.org/10.1590/0102-67202026000001e1930

article_title: "K" EY rules to improve learning skills in forth arm robotic platform.
citation: Bigolin AV, Cavazzola LT, Kalil AN. (2026). “K” EY rules to improve learning skills in forth arm robotic platform. ABCD Arq Bras Cir Dig. https://doi.org/10.1590/0102-67202026000001e1930
title: Four basic rules govern arm movement in the K technique
description: The article establishes "four main rules" for using the K technique: each quadrant can be occupied by one arm at a time; vacate the quadrant you want to occupy before activating the next arm; the arm closest to the optic changes position running medially; the most lateral arm changes position by rotating externally. These rules aim to avoid collisions and conflicts of function.
requirements: Rules apply to the side of the screen housing two working arms divided into three quadrants
constraints: Rule 3 applies to the arm closest to the optic and rule 4 to the most lateral arm (1 or 4)
examples: Video 1 and Video 2 standardize robotic maneuvers using the K rules

article_title: "K" EY rules to improve learning skills in forth arm robotic platform.
citation: Bigolin AV, Cavazzola LT, Kalil AN. (2026). “K” EY rules to improve learning skills in forth arm robotic platform. ABCD Arq Bras Cir Dig. https://doi.org/10.1590/0102-67202026000001e1930
title: The "K" technique as a training resource for four-arm robotic platforms
description: The "K" technique is a reproducible training methodology for the four-arm robotic platform, developed from the training of more than 400 surgeons. It offers "a simple and reproducible methodology for developing important skills to reduce the learning curve for new robotic surgeries", and serves as a practical tool for dry-lab and virtual reality training environments.
requirements: Practical training is essential; some skills can be trained in VR but dry-lab practice with a qualified instructor is needed
constraints: Dry-lab training is limited by availability of dedicated robotic platforms, cost of training arms, and instructor availability
examples: Recognized by students as the most effective activity in the training program
